correctness.rationale: The exact complex-gradient normalization yields symbol ψα(n)=n²B(n,α+1) for all integer modes. The beta first-difference identity gives the positive Poisson-mixture jump measure for 0<α≤1; the geometric-sum identity treats α=0. A pushforward of any hypothetical positive measure for α>1 would have Cesàro cosine averages converging to its mass, contradicted by ψα(n)→0 while ψα(1)>0, without symmetry assumptions. The mixing total mass and singular scalings are explicit; α=1 has ν1(dt)=dt and a rate-one compound Poisson generator. The first positive multiplier gives the sharp gap. The included checker passed 674 supplementary finite assertions. Infinite statements rest on the proof, not tests.
